token-check: Validates both the Outlook token via isTokenExpired() and the Supabase session via getSupabaseSession(). Bails immediately with an error object if either is missing or expired. Extracts userId from session.user.id for all downstream steps.
user-change-detection: Compares the current userId against lastSyncUserId stored in chrome.storage.local. If they differ (or on first run), resets lastSyncTime, connectedOutlookEmail, cachedFolders, and folderCacheTime to force a full catchup on account switch. Stores the new lastSyncUserId to prevent repeated resets.
profile-fetch: Fetches the user's profile from Supabase via getProfile(userId) to retrieve connected_outlook_email, onboarding_completed_at, and initial_sync_complete flags. Extracts outlookEmail from the token via getOutlookEmail(token.token). Profile data gates subsequent account-lock and sync-mode logic.
seed-folder-sync: Sets the in-memory flag hasCompletedFolderSync = true if profile.initial_sync_complete === true, restoring folder discovery state that would otherwise be lost when the MV3 service worker terminates. This allows subsequent syncs to skip DOM polling and use the cached folder list.
outlook-account-lock: On first sync (when profile.connected_outlook_email is null), locks the Outlook account by calling setConnectedOutlookEmail(userId, outlookEmail). On subsequent syncs, verifies the token account matches the lock and aborts with {error: "OUTLOOK_MISMATCH"} if it doesn't. Clears stale mismatch state on match or if no outlookEmail is found.
force-catchup-mode: During early onboarding (when onboarding_completed_at is null, lastSyncTime exists, and hasCompletedFolderSync is false), resets lastSyncTime = null if sync age is under 2 × EMAIL_SYNC_PERIOD_MIN (90 seconds). This forces the next fetch to use the larger MAX_CATCHUP_EMAILS limit rather than the incremental 50-email window.
set-email-cap: Determines the maxEmails per-folder cap: 200 if isInitialSync (onboarding incomplete AND folders not yet discovered), 50 if lastSyncTime exists (incremental mode), or MAX_CATCHUP_EMAILS for a full catchup. Logs the sync mode state for debugging.
folder-discovery: Calls discoverMailFolders() to read the Outlook sidebar DOM via chrome.scripting, returning subfolder IDs. Prepends a hardcoded Inbox entry (distinguished folder), filters duplicate "Inbox" results, and sets hasCompletedFolderSync = true on success. Fails silently and continues with inbox-only if the DOM is unreachable.
per-folder-fetch-push: Loops through each folder sequentially: handleGetEmails() → enrichEmailsBatched() → maps rows with user_id, email_ref, subject, sender, body (capped at 50 KB), recipients, etc. → pushEmails() to Supabase. Status defaults to "unprocessed" via DB trigger. Per-folder failures are non-blocking; the loop continues to the next folder.
sent-items-sync: Separate non-blocking fetch via handleGetSentItems() with the same maxSentEmails cap logic (50 if incremental, else MAX_CATCHUP_EMAILS). Enriches via enrichEmailsBatched(), transforms rows with status: "completed" (intentionally not queued for draft generation), and pushes to Supabase. Sent item failure doesn't block inbox sync completion.
persist-lastSyncTime: Sets lastSyncTime = new Date().toISOString() and calls persistSyncTime() to write to chrome.storage.local after all folder and sent fetches complete. Also stores lastSyncUserId to track account identity. This timestamp gates incremental vs. catchup mode in future cycles (steps 06 and 07).
alias-detection: Calls detectAndUpdateAliases(userId, authEmail, sentEnriched) using the auth email from session.user.email and sender addresses extracted from sent items. Updates profiles.user_email_aliases in Supabase so downstream classification can correctly identify the user's own messages.
heartbeat: Calls updateHeartbeat(userId) (errors caught silently via .catch(() => {})) to update profiles.last_heartbeat_at. The Python worker uses this timestamp to determine whether the extension is active — if stale for more than 15 minutes, the worker falls back to business-hours heuristics.
signal-initial-sync: If hasCompletedFolderSync === true AND profile.initial_sync_complete === false, calls setInitialSyncComplete(userId) to PATCH the flag to true in Supabase, gating the Phase B onboarding pipeline. Runs after ALL folder syncs complete to prevent the "flag set but emails not landed" race. Per-folder failures in step 09 are non-blocking, so partial folder coverage is possible — the email_count >= 500 gate in Phase B mitigates this.
get-users-needing-onboarding: Queries the profiles table with four gate conditions: onboarding_completed_at IS NULL, onboarding_status in {null, pending, failed}, initial_sync_complete = true, and email_count >= 500. Returns a list of eligible user IDs that haven't been onboarded yet, filtering out users still syncing or with insufficient email volume for meaningful profiling.
run-onboarding: Invokes run_onboarding(db, uid, profile) from runner.py, which executes the full three-stage onboarding pipeline. Sets onboarding_status to "running" on entry. Edge case: if the function crashes before completion, status remains "running" and blocks all future attempts — the stuck-onboarding recovery in _recover_stuck_onboarding() resets these to "pending" on worker restart.
collect-emails: Calls collect_onboarding_emails() which fetches up to 1500 emails over 180 days, filters spam/noise using blacklist senders (noreply@, mailer-daemon@, etc.) and subject patterns (accepted:, declined:, etc.), removes calendar invites (iCalendar content) and empty bodies (<10 chars), then caps at 500. Fatal: fewer than 10 received emails aborts immediately with status "failed".
style-gate: If fewer than 30 sent emails exist, sets skip_guides = True. Onboarding continues without style or behavioral guides. This cascades downstream: style guide synthesis requires ≥15 features (MIN_STYLE_FEATURES), and behavioral synthesis requires ≥10 features (MIN_BEHAVIORAL_FEATURES). All guide dependencies fail gracefully, enabling partial onboarding (complete_partial status).
stats-extraction: Calls extract_all() which runs pure-Python analysis on 180 days of collected emails: extracts response_events (reply counts, timing), threads (message grouping), domains, and per-contact frequencies (frequency, reply rates, avg_response_time_hours, response_rate_30d/90d, smoothed_rate). Builds the baseline user_topic_profile (aggregate statistics, no AI). Returns a structured extraction dict.
persist-stage1: Writes Stage 1 extraction results to DB: upsert_response_events(), upsert_threads(), upsert_domains(), upsert_contacts() (stats-only, no AI enrichment yet), and the baseline topic_profile. Fatal: any write failure sets status "failed" and aborts. If all succeed, core user data persists before AI phases begin (graceful degradation).
contact-synthesis: Calls synthesize_contacts() which aggregates per-contact stats (frequency, reply_rate, avg_response_time) with Haiku extractions (email type, keywords), then submits to Sonnet to infer up to 50 contact profiles with org, role, expertise_areas, contact_type, relationship_significance, and relationship_summary. Non-fatal fallback: if Sonnet fails, uses _fallback_contact_profiles() (stats-only, no enrichment).
persist-stage2: Writes all AI enrichments to DB: upsert_topic_profile(), update_writing_style(), update_behavioral_profile(), update_preference_profile() (JSONB column). Tracks missing_components (style_guide, behavioral_profile) for degraded completion status. Preference profile absence does not degrade status — it's an optional additive layer.
train-classifier: Calls train_user_model(db, user_id) which fetches response_events (requires ≥30 events, uses defaults if insufficient), computes global_rate (fraction of emails responded to), derives lift factors from boolean features (user_position, subject_type, msg_type, recipient_count_bins, thread_depth_bins), detects recurring patterns (cadence, same-sender sequences), fits isotonic regression, and computes triage thresholds (hard_gate at 0.01, soft_gate at 0.03). Stores scoring_parameters JSON to profiles table. Non-fatal on failure.
mark-existing-emails: Bulk updates all emails that were part of the onboarding sample to status "onboarding". This prevents them from being picked up by accumulate_emails() in Phase D. Only emails arriving after this step will be processed for drafts.
mark-complete: Sets onboarding_status to "complete" (or "complete_partial" if style_guide or behavioral_profile is missing) and writes onboarding_completed_at timestamp. complete_partial is set when style or behavioral guides are missing (skip_guides was true, or synthesis failed). A missing preference profile does NOT trigger complete_partial — the preference layer is additive. Setting onboarding_completed_at is the gate that unlocks Phase D normal processing.
accumulate-emails: Only runs for onboarded users. Picks up emails that arrived after step 26 (status="unprocessed"). For each email: runs signal extraction (5 Haiku signals via Anthropic Batches API), applies the chain-of-thought draft generation with the three-layer profile (style + behavioral + preference), and writes the draft. The preference profile is loaded alongside the other two guides and injected into the draft prompt. If preference_profile is null, the preference section is simply omitted. QC check validates greeting/sign-off presence and word count; retries once with revision notes on failure.
